title: Site Migration Failures
description: Fix broken sites after migration — wrong URLs, missing media, broken permalinks, serialized data corruption, and DNS issues.

steps.title: Document Post-Migration Symptoms
steps.instructions: List broken images, wrong links, 404s, login failures, or layout issues. Note migration tool used and whether database or files were migrated separately.

steps.title: Run Safe Search-Replace on URLs
steps.instructions: Use Better Search Replace or WP-CLI on staging first. Replace old domain with new (http and https variants). Never blind replace in production without backup.

steps.title: Update siteurl and home Options
steps.instructions: Set correct URLs in Settings → General or wp-config.php constants (WP_HOME, WP_SITEURL). Mismatched URLs break logins, assets, and REST API.

steps.title: Fix Corrupted Serialized Data
steps.instructions: Naive search-replace breaks serialized PHP strings in options and meta. Use serialization-aware tools only. Symptoms: broken widgets, theme settings, page builder data.

steps.title: Flush Permalinks and Rewrite Rules
steps.instructions: Visit Settings → Permalinks and save. Re-assign WooCommerce pages and menu locations if they broke after import.

steps.title: Verify Media Files Migrated
steps.instructions: Confirm wp-content/uploads copied completely. Broken images often mean incomplete file transfer or wrong upload URL in database.

steps.title: Confirm DNS and SSL on New Host
steps.instructions: Verify A/CNAME records point to new server. Install SSL certificate and update URLs to https. Test before switching production DNS if possible.

steps.title: Full Site Verification Checklist
steps.instructions: Test homepage, internal links, forms, checkout, admin login, and email delivery. Run a broken link checker before announcing migration complete.
